title: Functorial K-injective Hom and scalar telescopes agree on every leg
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and assume filtered colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], integer-indexed cochain complexes and the localization $Q$ to their unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $s$ be a global section of $R$, and let $A,P$ be arbitrary complexes of $R$-module sheaves. Fix a functorial K-injective resolution $i_B:B\to I(B)$ as in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-pur-kinjective-complex]; the functor $I$ is not assumed $R$-linear. Form the internal Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex]
$$X=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(A,I(P)),$$
and its chain endomorphisms $t_1=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(A,I(s_P))$ and $t_2=s_X$, where $s_P,s_X$ denote multiplication by $s$. Then $t_1$ and $t_2$ are chain-homotopic. For $k=1,2$ let $C_k$ be the termwise colimit of $X\xrightarrow{t_k}X\xrightarrow{t_k}\cdots$, with colimit legs $j_n^{(k)}:X\to C_k$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. There exists an isomorphism
$$\gamma:Q(C_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C_2)\quad\text{such that}\quad\gamma\circ Q(j_n^{(1)})=Q(j_n^{(2)})\quad(n\geq0).$$
Thus the tower obtained by applying the fixed functorial internal-Hom representative $\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(A,I(-))$ to $(P,s_P)$ and the scalar tower on $X$ have isomorphic colimits in $D(R)$, with this compatibility for every leg, including the zeroth. Neither $A$, $P$, nor $X$ is required to be bounded, and no continuity hypothesis on derived internal Hom is imposed.
